主要内容: LKQ Corporation, a leading provider of alternative vehicle replacement products, operates through three segments: Wholesale—North America, Wholesale—Europe, and Self Service. The company distributes a variety of products to collision and mechanical repair shops, including aftermarket, recycled, refurbished, and remanufactured items. LKQ is the largest provider of alternative vehicle collision replacement products in the U.S. and a leading provider of mechanical replacement products in the U.K. and Canada. The company sources most of its aftermarket inventory from U.S., Taiwan, European, and Chinese manufacturers. Recycled products are obtained by purchasing salvaged vehicles and dismantling them. LKQ also sells refurbished and remanufactured products like wheels, bumper covers, lights, and engines. The company's primary customers are collision and mechanical repair shops, with indirect reliance on insurance companies to drive demand. LKQ has pursued growth through acquisitions, including 16 during the nine months ended September 30, 2013, with significant investments in European and North American markets. Notable acquisitions include Sator Beheer BV, a leading distributor of auto parts, tools, and equipment in the Netherlands, acquired for approximately $268 million. LKQ's 3 operating segments include its North American aftermarket equipment and accessories business, which involves Keystone Automotive Operations, Inc. (a distributor and marketer of specialty aftermarket equipment and accessories in North America). LKQ acquired Keystone for $450 million. Keystone has over 1,500 employees, with 25 locations serving more than 20,000 specialty retailers and equipment installers throughout North America, offering a broad product line of over 300,000 SKUs from over 800 suppliers. LKQ stated that the entire specialty aftermarket equipment and accessories industry is a highly fragmented $31 billion market, and Keystone's current product categories represent about $5 billion of the industry. Keystone's revenue for 2014 is expected to be approximately $700 million, with an EBITDA margin of approximately 10%. LKQ noted that the North American market continues to grow in geography and product offerings. Alternative Parts Usage (APU) trends are favorable, certified parts continue to grow, vehicle procurement dynamics are improving, and macro trends (such as miles driven, unemployment, and gas prices) are trending in the company's favor. These dynamics, coupled with LKQ's first-mover advantage on technological initiatives such as the CCC ONE integration, have positioned the company's North American operations well for 2014 and beyond. LKQ's peer, Advance Auto Parts, Inc. (AAP), saw its shares rise recently after it completed the acquisition of General Parts International, Inc. (GPII) for $2.04 billion. The deal will create one of the largest providers of aftermarket auto parts in North America, with $9.2 billion in annual sales. This is just above the sales of the leading player, Autozone (AZO).
